Imagine standing in a glass box 103 floors above Chicago when the floor under you starts to crack.
Most people think the glass is breaking and they're about to fall.
But this floor is three layers of tempered glass pressed into one solid slab.
It's heated and then blasted with cold air which makes it four times stronger than normal glass.
On top sits a thin clear coating that keeps millions of shoes from scratching it.
And if something hits it too hard that coating is made to crack first so the glass below doesn't.
That's what happened in 2019 when it splintered into thousands of pieces right under people's feet.
It looked like the floor was giving out but the glass underneath never broke.
Even cracked that floor can still hold five tons.
That's like parking two and a half cars on a glass shelf 1,300 feet in the air.
